jobs.description:

As a leading partner in healthcare, Medline Canada's sole purpose is to make healthcare run better
– this means being deeply committed to the health and well-being of our customers, employees, partners and our communities. We employ a diverse group of top talent focused on growing and making a difference in the lives of Canadians, coast-to-coast.

Job Description Summary

The Vice President, Sales Operations is a key member of the Canadian leadership team responsible for building and leading the operational infrastructure, insights, processes and capabilities that enable the sales organization to grow efficiently and profitably.

This role provides strategic leadership across Sales Operations functions including sales compensation, commercial analytics, pricing support, customer data, CRM effectiveness, customer implementation, sales productivity, segmentation, territory and coverage optimization, and automation.

Working closely with Sales, Finance, Marketing, IT, Customer Service, Supply Chain and other cross-functional partners, the Vice President will translate Medline Canada's commercial strategy into scalable processes, actionable insights and measurable operating disciplines. The role has particular accountability for improving sales productivity, strengthening pricing and gross margin management, optimizing sales coverage across channels, and ensuring the organization has the data and tools required to make effective commercial decisions.

Job Description

Sales Strategy, Productivity & Commercial Excellence

Partner with senior Sales and Canadian leadership to translate commercial strategy into effective sales operating models, processes, performance measures and execution plans.
Establish a comprehensive sales productivity framework, including productivity by sales channel, territory, customer segment and revenue base.
Lead sales segmentation analysis to ensure resources are aligned to the highest-value opportunities and appropriate customer segments.
Assess sales coverage and capacity across Canada, identifying areas of over- or under-coverage and opportunities to improve productivity.
Develop territory and coverage models that consider traditional field sales as well as evolving channels, particularly eCommerce and digital customer engagement.
Establish regular operating reviews that provide leadership with visibility to sales productivity, commercial performance, operational bottlenecks and emerging risks.
Partner with Sales leadership to simplify administrative work and increase customer-facing and selling time.

Sales Compensation & Performance Management

Provide executive oversight of sales compensation administration, governance and reporting.
Ensure sales compensation programs are administered accurately and on time, supported by clear service standards, controls and escalation processes.
Develop reporting that identifies sales compensation trends, exceptions and potential areas of concern.
Partner with Sales, Finance and Human Resources to ensure compensation programs support commercial strategy, desired sales behaviours and organizational priorities.
Strengthen controls, processes and automation related to compensation administration.

Commercial Analytics & Business Intelligence

Lead the Commercial Business Analyst function and establish analytics capabilities that enable faster, data-driven commercial decision-making.
Develop dashboards and reporting for sales performance, productivity, segmentation, customer revenue, pricing and gross margin.
Ensure commercial leaders have timely and consistent access to actionable business insights.
Improve bid management processes and monitor bid cycle time, quality and capacity.
Establish standardized metrics and definitions to create consistent commercial reporting across the Canadian organization.
Move reporting beyond historical results toward forward-looking insights, trends, and identification of sales opportunities and risks.

Pricing & Gross Margin Management

Provide leadership oversight for Medline Brand pricing processes and commercial pricing governance.
Establish appropriate pricing and gross margin checkpoints for large or strategically significant contracts, ensuring visibility to financial impact before commercial commitments are finalized.
Partner closely with Sales and Finance to balance revenue growth, customer competitiveness and gross margin performance.
Improve pricing efficiency through standardized approval rules, automation and exception management.
Monitor quote auto-approval, contract price activation and related pricing service measures.
Identify trends in pricing, discounts and margin performance and recommend corrective actions where appropriate.

CRM, Data & Sales Technology

Provide leadership and governance over CRM processes, adoption and effectiveness.
Ensure the CRM environment supports sales execution, pipeline visibility, forecasting and customer management without creating unnecessary administrative burden.
Establish measurable CRM adoption and process-engagement standards, including monitoring opportunity management and auto-close activity.
Lead improvements to customer and sales data quality, governance and accessibility.
Oversee customer-data processes to support timely and accurate new customer account setup.
Partner with IT and business stakeholders to integrate systems, simplify workflows and automate manual activities.

Automation & Process Improvement

Develop a Sales Operations automation roadmap focused on reducing manual activity, accelerating cycle times, improving accuracy and increasing sales productivity.
Identify high-volume or repetitive processes suitable for workflow automation, system integration or self-service.
Establish measures to quantify the productivity, capacity and financial benefits generated through automation.
Promote continuous improvement and process standardization across Sales Operations functions.

Customer Implementation

Oversee the commercial implementation process for new business and significant customer transitions.
Partner cross-functionally to identify and resolve implementation bottlenecks and improve customer onboarding.
Establish and monitor differentiated implementation cycle-time expectations for the Acute and Post-Acute businesses.
Develop reporting that highlights implementation performance by sales office, business segment and customer type.
Ensure clear ownership and escalation processes exist for complex implementations.

Leadership & Organizational Capability

Build and lead a high-performing, analytically strong Sales Operations organization.
Establish clear accountability, performance expectations and development plans across the function.
Develop talent and succession pipelines for critical Sales Operations capabilities.
Foster a culture of data-driven decision-making, continuous improvement, accountability and cross-functional partnership.
Serve as a trusted strategic advisor to Canadian Sales and executive leadership, bringing fact-based recommendations and constructive challenge to commercial decisions.
Lead change-management efforts associated with new sales processes, technology, operating models and productivity initiatives.

Key Measures of Success

Accurate and timely sales compensation administration, supported by effective controls and transparent trend reporting.
Efficient bid-cycle management and improved responsiveness to commercial opportunities.
Effective Medline Brand pricing processes, including streamlined approvals and timely contract price activation.
Timely and accurate customer account setup and strong customer-data governance.
Consistent, well-managed customer implementations across the Acute and Post-Acute businesses.
Meaningful CRM process engagement, reliable pipeline data and disciplined opportunity management.
Improved sales productivity and clear performance visibility by channel, territory, customer segment and revenue base.
Optimized sales coverage and capacity, including effective support for eCommerce and digital channels.
Appropriate pricing and gross margin governance for major contracts.
Demonstrable productivity and capacity gains generated through automation and process improvement.

Qualifications

Education & Experience

Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Economics, Analytics, Commerce or a related discipline; an MBA or other advanced business degree is an asset.
Significant progressive experience in Sales Operations, Commercial Excellence, Revenue Operations, Finance, Commercial Analytics or a related function.
Senior leadership experience leading multiple Sales Operations or commercial support disciplines.
Demonstrated experience supporting a large, complex, multi-channel sales organization.
Strong background in sales productivity, sales compensation, commercial analytics, pricing and margin management.
Experience developing customer segmentation, territory design, coverage and capacity models.
Demonstrated success improving and automating complex commercial processes.
Experience within medical devices, healthcare distribution, pharmaceuticals, B2B distribution or another complex commercial environment is preferred.

Knowledge & Skills

Strong commercial and financial acumen, including a practical understanding of revenue, gross margin, pricing and profitability.
Advanced analytical capability with the ability to convert complex data into clear commercial recommendations.
Strong understanding of CRM platforms, sales analytics and business intelligence tools.
Demonstrated ability to develop executive-level dashboards, performance measures and operating reviews.
Strong process-improvement mindset with experience driving automation and productivity.
Excellent communication and influencing skills, with the ability to work effectively across Sales, Finance, Human Resources, Marketing, IT, Supply Chain and operational functions.
Strong change leadership and organizational capability-building skills.
Ability to balance strategic leadership with disciplined operational execution.
Demonstrated ability to lead through complexity, prioritize competing business needs and drive accountability across functions.

Leadership Profile

The successful candidate will be a commercially minded, data-driven leader who can see both the big picture and the operating mechanics behind it. They will understand how sales coverage, compensation, pricing, CRM, customer data, implementation and analytics connect to drive revenue productivity and profitable growth.

They will be comfortable challenging existing processes, using data to influence senior leaders, and moving the organization toward a more automated, scalable and insight-driven Sales Operations model.

jobs.title: Director, Enterprise Architecture
jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Director of Enterprise Architecture is a strategic leadership role responsible for defining and advancing SE Health’s enterprise architecture vision. This position establishes architecture discipline as a cornerstone of SE Health’s modernization strategy by aligning technology capabilities with business priorities, enabling digital transformation, and ensuring successful integration of critical platforms such as the digital patient record, people/finance/payroll systems, contact center, service management, and others.

The Director leads enterprise-wide architecture decisions that drive agility, scalability, security, and measurable business outcomes. This includes building and maturing the Enterprise Architecture function, establishing an Architecture Review Board, and delivering a three-year technology roadmap that incorporates strategic platforms, cloud strategy, data and analytics capabilities, integration architecture, and security and compliance posture. The Director ensures successful architecture and integration of platforms such as Alayacare and Workday, while driving adoption of best practices, standards, and governance across technology domains. By translating business objectives into coherent, secure, and sustainable technology designs, the Director plays a critical role in spearheading a digital transformation that enhances the experience of patients, families, employees, and clients, supporting SE Health’s mission of exceptional home and community care.

Primary Accountabilities

Enterprise Architecture Strategy and Governance

Develop and execute an enterprise architecture strategy and multi-year roadmap that enables modernization, interoperability, and alignment with organizational goals, including maximizing value from core enterprise platforms (e.g., Alayacare, Workday).
Establish and lead enterprise architecture governance processes (e.g., an Architecture Review Board or Enterprise Architecture Council) to define standards, manage technical debt, and inform major technology and investment decisions.
Serve as a strategic advisor to the CDO, CIO, CTO, and senior leadership, translating business priorities into sustainable, secure, enterprise-wide technology designs.
Assess and improve enterprise architecture maturity, documenting improvements and outcomes aligned to business KPIs and informing continuous evolution of architecture practices.
Drive mission-critical enterprise architecture and data modernization projects, providing strategic oversight and ensuring integration, scalability, and compliance across platforms and business functions.

Technology, Cloud and Systems Integration Architecture

Lead the architecture, integration, and modernization of core enterprise platforms, including Alayacare, Workday, Procura, ERP, CRM, HRIS, Finance, and scheduling systems, to enable a cohesive and interoperable ecosystem across business and clinical operations.
Define and oversee enterprise reference architectures, integration and data standards, patterns, and roadmaps that promote modernization, automation, analytics enablement, and business process optimization.
Lead modernization efforts to rationalize applications, reduce technical debt, and migrate or retire legacy platforms using a cloud-smart, scalable approach.
Oversee enterprise solution architecture across cloud, hybrid, and on-premises environments to ensure performance, resilience, security, and cost-efficiency, including multi-cloud strategy across AWS and Azure.
Guide adoption of architectural best practices across security, operational excellence, reliability, performance efficiency, and cost optimization domains.
Review and evaluate solution designs and technology proposals, providing direction and recommendations through architecture governance forums.
Analyze enterprise technology and data architecture requirements to support new applications, system scalability, and platform integrations.

Leadership, People and Continuous Improvement

Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing enterprise architecture team, fostering a culture of collaboration, innovation, and excellence.
Drive continuous improvement and EA maturity by introducing modern frameworks, methodologies, and tooling (e.g., TOGAF, HOPEX) to enhance consistency, documentation, and solution quality.
Embed security and privacy by design across architecture practices, ensuring adherence to cybersecurity, privacy, and healthcare compliance requirements.
Build strong partnerships with Digital, Security, and Business leaders to influence technology strategy, support demand intake, and ensure alignment of solutions to business needs.
Champion digital transformation and innovation by evaluating emerging technologies (e.g., mobile, IoT, telehealth, AI) and recommending their adoption where they advance SE Health’s mission and services.

Data and Analytics Architecture

Define enterprise data architecture strategies, standards, and models that enable analytics, AI, and data-driven decision-making across the organization.
Partner with Data & Analytics teams to design and evolve data platforms (e.g., data lake/warehouse) to support enterprise information management, governance, reporting, and advanced analytics.
Provide leadership, guidance, and mentoring to data architecture and solution design teams on data and integration best practices.
Collaborate with data science and analytics teams to support AI-enabled insights, intelligent automation, and emerging technologies that drive value for clinical and business functions.

AI, Automation & Intelligent Systems

Lead integration of AI-driven insights and intelligent automation into enterprise applications and workflows.
Partner with data science teams to enable machine learning, predictive analytics, and data-driven optimization across clinical and business functions.
Evaluate emerging AI/automation technologies and define architectural guardrails for safe, ethical, and scalable adoption.

Qualifications & Experience

Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Systems, or related field. Experience with EA frameworks (e.g., TOGAF, ArchiMate, or similar) is preferred.
12+ years of experience in enterprise/solution architecture, including leading modernization and large-scale integration initiatives in complex environments.
5+ years of leadership experience managing architecture teams, building high-performing technical talent, and advancing enterprise architecture maturity.
Strong expertise across enterprise, application, data, and technology architecture, with hands-on experience in cloud and integration architectures (AWS/Azure, APIs, microservices, event-driven design).
Experience leading architecture for major SaaS platforms (e.g., CRM, ERP, HR systems); Alayacare and/or Workday strongly preferred.
Strong understanding of data architecture, governance, and analytics enablement; experience with AI/ML-enabled solutions is an asset.
Knowledge of security, privacy, and compliance considerations for enterprise platforms and data.
Experience in healthcare or other highly regulated industries is an asset.
Exceptional communication, consulting, and stakeholder engagement skills, with proven ability to influence executives and simplify complex concepts for diverse audiences.

Why join SE Health?

Competitive Total Rewards So much more than a paycheque! Enjoy comprehensive benefits, pension, flexible pay options, car-loan support, housing solutions and exclusive staff perks.
Flexibility & Belonging Thrive with hybrid work, flexible scheduling and a supportive, inclusive culture that puts people first.
Purpose & Impact Join a national social enterprise where your voice matters. Every role helps advance health, spark innovation and strengthen communities across Canada.
Growth That Meets Your Ambition Access tuition support, training and meaningful career pathways across a growing, future-focused organization.

SE Health is a not-for-profit social enterprise advancing health with heart. With 115+ years of impact, we bring hope, happiness and exceptional care to people and communities across Canada. We lead with empathy, dignity and purpose while building a future where everyone can realize their full health and well-being potential. We’re also an inclusive, supportive workplace offering competitive compensation, strong benefits and real opportunities to grow. We’re All In Together.

Build the commercial engine that powers profitable growth.

Reporting to the Chief Commercial Officer, the Vice-President, Revenue Operations & Commercial Excellence is a transformational executive leader responsible for building the capabilities, insights, governance and operating disciplines that enable predictable, profitable growth across the organization. As a key strategic partner to the executive team, you will connect commercial strategy, planning, pricing, analytics, technology and execution across the customer lifecycle, creating a unified view of performance that enables smarter decisions and stronger business outcomes across North America.

This role is ideal for a strategic and commercially minded leader who excels at translating complexity into action. You bring a balance of analytical rigor, operational excellence and change leadership, along with the ability to influence across functions, build high-performing teams and drive enterprise-wide alignment. Leveraging data, customer insights and business performance indicators, you will help shape the commercial capabilities, processes and ways of working that accelerate growth, improve productivity and strengthen profitability.

What You'll Do:

Lead enterprise-wide commercial planning, forecasting and performance management processes, ensuring alignment between growth objectives, resource priorities and financial outcomes.
Build and maintain a consolidated view of commercial performance, customer trends, risks and opportunities to enable timely, data-driven decision-making.
Develop executive scorecards, operating reviews and performance reporting that provide visibility into growth, retention, productivity and profitability.
Lead scenario planning and commercial modelling activities to support strategic investments, resource allocation decisions and growth initiatives.
Establish pricing strategies, governance frameworks and decision guardrails that strengthen price realization, improve margin performance and support sustainable growth.
Partner closely with Commercial, Finance and Operations leaders to improve forecasting accuracy, demand visibility and business planning effectiveness.
Advance commercial analytics and business intelligence capabilities by partnering with Data & Analytics and IT to strengthen reporting, governance and decision support.
Champion predictive analytics, automation and AI-enabled solutions that improve productivity, enhance data quality and accelerate decision-making.
Shape the commercial technology roadmap, ensuring CRM, analytics and other commercial platforms are integrated, scalable and aligned to business needs.
Establish common commercial processes, governance structures and operating rhythms that improve consistency, accountability and execution across functions.

Who We Are

Every day, people around the world take medicine, pour a drink, wash their hands, wear a fragrance, or fill up their car. Most of them never think about what’s inside. We do, because a lot of it starts with us.

Greenfield Global produces the high-purity alcohols, specialty solvents, custom blends, bioprocessing inputs, and low-carbon fuels that industries in more than 50 countries depend on. Founded in 1989 as a single plant in Tiverton, Ontario, we now operate ethanol distilleries in Ontario and Québec, manufacturing and packaging facilities in Canada, the United States, and Ireland, and a globally integrated supply chain. Because we’re the producer and not a middleman, we control every step from sourcing and testing to delivery, giving customers exceptional quality, reliability, and support.

About The Role

The Vice President (VP), Supply and Trading leads the commercial supply and trading activities of the Renewable Energy business unit, with a focus on renewable fuels and related environmental markets. Build, lead, and develop a high-performing supply and trading team.

Approve feedstock and co-product strategies on behalf of Renewable Energy.
Lead logistics strategy of the Renewable Energy supply network.
Develop and maintain hedging strategies and risk policies in partnership with Finance and Risk.
Support offtake strategy and commercial structuring for new products, including e-methanol and other low-carbon molecules.
Track and interpret policy and market developments (CFR, LCFS, the European Renewable Energy Directive, and provincial mandates) and translate them into commercial positioning.
Provide market intelligence, forecasts, and performance reporting to Renewable Energy executive leadership.

At least 12 years in energy, biofuels, or commodity trading, including at least five in a senior leadership role.
Deep knowledge of ethanol and low-carbon fuel markets and environmental credit programs.

Strong commercial negotiation and structuring skills; experience with long-term offtake or supply agreements is an asset.
Bachelor’s degree in business, engineering, economics, or a related field.
Functional in English and French.
Demonstrated ability to take full ownership and accountability for decisions, results, and business outcomes.

Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to communicate complex issues clearly, directly, and effectively at all levels of the organization.
Strong and decisive leadership, with the ability to set direction, make difficult decisions, and lead with conviction.
Strong executive presence and demonstrated ability to influence, engage, and mobilize others.

Improved margin capture and reduced volatility.

jobs.description:
THE OPPORTUNITY

We have an excellent opportunity to join a progressive Alberta school division as Director of Finance, based in Edmonton. Reporting to the Superintendent, the Director of Finance serves as the Division’s senior financial officer and leads finance administration across the organization and works directly with the Board of Trustees and its committees.

This role oversees the Division’s financial accounting, reporting, budgeting and works collaboratively with business operations in assisting in making sound business decisions. Its core areas include building the annual budget and capital plan, supporting the Board, managing contracts, agreements and partnerships.

The Division is committed to continuous improvement and continues to invest in its processes, technology and systems. This role offers real room to learn, grow and lead within an organization grounded in strong values and a deep commitment to Indigenous education. Regular travel to Division’s schools and communities is part of this role and may sometimes involve extended stays.

THE IDEAL CANDIDATE

The ideal candidate is a highly capable senior finance leader with a solid understanding of Board governance and the statutory and regulatory framework that school divisions work within. Progressive and motivated, this individual believes strongly in public education and in the Division’s purpose and guiding values.

The successful candidate brings a strong work ethic, a drive for excellence and continuous improvement, and a strong sense of accountability for both personal and team results. Collaborative and focused on practical solutions, this leader cares about service and has excellent organizational, technical, interpersonal and communication skills, along with the ability to resolve conflict. Equally at ease in a political setting with an elected Board of Trustees, the Director of Finance will build productive relationships with Alberta Education and Childcare, other provincial ministries and community partners.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Financial Leadership and Planning

Serving as the Division’s senior financial officer, ensuring that funding received is accurate and used according to its terms and conditions, and that operations remain fiscally sound.
Preparing financial statements, accountability reports and other required reports, coordinating the annual external audit, and making sure all legal, Ministerial and Board requirements, deadlines and Superintendent directives are met.
Directing the Division’s accounting and financial reporting, including full cycle accounting, accounts payable and accounts receivable, general ledger oversight, corporate card programs, the chart of accounts, capital and project ledgers, the fixed assets register and financial advisory support.
Direct Supervision of the Division’s financial analyst
Leading annual budget development under the Superintendent’s direction and in line with the Division’s education plan and Board guidelines, setting budget processes that meet provincial requirements and allow for stakeholder input, and preparing budget submissions, forecasts and analysis for senior administration and the Board.
Building a comprehensive budget process for every school and department, tracking grants and special project funds, and supporting principals and department heads with their budgets, grant requirements and financial affairs.
Serving as signing authority with the Board Chair and Superintendent on all financial and investing surplus funds as permitted by Board policy.
Overseeing payroll so that it reflects the Division’s values, and reviewing and approving all operating, capital and payroll expenditures as the finance officer.

Board Governance and Corporate Secretary

Co-managing all Board, committee and public meetings, with the Superintendent of Schools & CEO and the Associate Superintendent of Corporate Services. Also, from giving notice and preparing agenda packages with the Superintendent of Schools & CEO to attending meetings.
Interpreting legislation that affects Division operations, including the Education Act.
To be familiar with and apply the yearly funding manual to business operations and budget
Upholding the Board’s role as set out in Board policy, helping the Superintendent develop and review Board policy, and leading administrative procedures and policy interpretation for areas of responsibility.

Systems, Controls and Purchasing

Owning the ERP accounting platform, including data management, security, workflows and backups, and leading improvements to accounting policies, systems and processes.
Maintaining the internal audit and risk management functions
Leading the purchasing function, keeping purchasing policies and systems efficient, maintaining inventory and appraisal records, and approving changes to the vendor master.
Negotiating and co- managing tuition and transportation agreements with external partners for Board approval and making sure all contracts and partnership agreements are properly completed.

Leadership and Relationships

Leading the Division’s finance team, giving direct reports clear direction, assessing performance and developing staff through coaching, mentoring and training.
Working with Human Resources on support staff hiring, staff development and business training for school staff, and supporting the Board’s bargaining committees.
Building a strong working relationship with the Superintendent, providing the financial advice and information needed for sound decisions, and contributing to the Executive Team and its committees.
Making sure parents, staff and school leaders receive responsive service, keeping communication open and transparent, and helping resolve concerns and conflicts.
Helping build a division culture that delivers results and handles emergencies as one team, and taking on other duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS

Bachelor’s or master’s degree in accounting, business or financial management. A CPA designation is required.
At least five (5) years of management experience, including supervising staff, managing performance and leading projects. Three (3) or more years of school division experience is an asset.
Eligibility for membership with ASBOA (Association of School Business Officials of Alberta). The ASBOA Certified School Business Official designation is an asset.
Thorough knowledge of accounting, financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, audit and financial operations.
Working knowledge of Board governance
Experience in contract management or purchasing.
Solid understanding of modern ERP and financial systems, including workflows, processes and data requirements.

KEY COMPETENCIES

Sound financial judgement, with the ability to build and manage budgets, produce financial statements and balance accounting standards, management information needs and government regulation.
Strong business sense grounded in current practices and a commitment to strategic planning, with a clear grasp of where the Division is headed over the long term and the ability to spot improvements and bring sound recommendations to the Board and the Superintendent.
Political acumen, with comfort working alongside an elected Board and other elected officials and the ability to work effectively with Alberta Education and Childcare and other provincial ministries.
Leadership that earns the trust and support of colleagues, with the ability to lead, coach and mentor a team and guide it through change.
Excellent interpersonal skills and strong written, verbal and listening skills, with the ability to work well with leaders at every level, including those from education and academic backgrounds, and to communicate clearly with staff, trustees, government officials and community members.
Creative problem solving, fresh thinking and a strong focus on service.
Strong ethics and integrity, with discretion in handling sensitive and confidential matters.

The Director, Technology Operations owns the operational health of the platforms Goway sells and services travel on: our reservations platform, the infrastructure it runs on, the supplier, air and distribution integrations it depends on, and the automation and data pipelines built around it.

What will be your key responsibilities?

Reliability and service management

Define, publish and report service levels and service-level objectives for revenue-critical services, starting with quoting, booking, payment and traveller servicing.
Own incident management end to end: severity definitions, escalation, incident command, communication during an incident, and post-incident review with corrective actions.
Own RCA and problem management.
Own change and release management as a company standard, balancing delivery throughput against change failure rate.
Build observability sufficient to detect degradation.
Own disaster recovery and business continuity for platform services, tested and documented on a stated cadence.

Integration and supplier platform operations

Monitoring of integration paths, error and failure-rate thresholds, and defined fallback behaviour when a partner degrades.
Maintain a dependency map of the external platforms our revenue-generating flows rely on, with assessed operational risk and mitigation for each.
Own operational readiness for new integrations and new product lines entering the platform.
Own the operational reliability of automation and data pipelines in production.

Platform and cloud operations

Day-to-day operation of the AWS and managed hosting infrastructure serving our platform estate: environments, provisioning, patching and lifecycle management.
Own hosting cost governance: visibility by service, a unit-cost measure, and an annual optimisation target.
Lead capacity planning against forecast booking and travel volumes.
Reduce manual, repeatable operational work through automation.
Address seasonal capacity planning, change freezes and enhanced coverage aligned to our booking and departure peaks and to new product launches.

Vendors, partners and compliance

Platform, hosting and integration partner relationships: SLA definition, enforcement and structured performance review.
Reduce single points of dependency, whether on a vendor or an individual.
Partner with security on vulnerability management, patch compliance, access control and audit readiness.

Build and maintain a multi-year technical operations roadmap aligned to Goway's growth plans.
Report operational performance, risk and investment needs to the CTO and executive team in business terms.

Ability to set standards and drive adoption across teams.

Infrastructure-as-code and container orchestration experience.
AWS Certified DevOps Engineer (Professional), or AWS Certified CloudOps Engineer (Associate). Solutions Architect certifications are welcome, but less relevant to this role than the operations-focused ones.

UBC Facilities is responsible for the planning, development, renewal and renovation of campus facilities, providing stewardship for all institutional facilities projects, including Housing and Athletics projects, at UBC s Vancouver and Okanagan campuses. Work Performed

Provides strategic leadership for the services offered by the Capital Planning & Development division, which includes capital planning, capital project development and oversight services for the University’s academic, administrative and ancillary infrastructure.

We're Ditto, a Toronto-based tech startup building a consumer mobile app designed to make everyday life a little more connected.

We are preparing for a new phase of our product and are looking for a technical leader to join our founding team, take ownership of our technology and help us build a scalable, data-driven platform.
We're a small team with big ambitions, and we're looking for someone who wants to build a company, not just write code.

We're looking for a hands-on CTO with a strong technical background, an entrepreneurial mindset and the ability to turn business and product ambitions into solid technical solutions.

Ideally, you're a full-stack developer
who's comfortable working across the entire technology stack, from building intuitive user experiences to designing backend architecture and data infrastructure.

Our technology stack is built around React
, and we're particularly interested in someone with a strong understanding of data pipelines, event tracking and product analytics.

We don't just want to build features. We want to understand how people use them, why they use them and how we can make them better.

Technical Strategy:
Own and define Ditto's technical vision, architecture and technology roadmap.
Full-Stack Development:
Actively contribute to frontend and backend development, integrations and infrastructure.
React Development:
Maintain, improve and expand our existing application.
Data Architecture & Pipelines:
Design reliable infrastructure for collecting, processing, storing and leveraging product data.
Event Tracking & Analytics:
Implement tracking mechanisms that enable us to understand user behaviour, engagement, conversion and retention.
Scalability:
Build a technical foundation that supports our growth without needing to rebuild everything six months later.
Security & Reliability:
Ensure our platform follows sound practices around security, privacy, performance and maintainability.
Product Collaboration:
Work closely with the product and marketing teams to translate business objectives into technical solutions.
Technical Leadership:
Shape our engineering culture and eventually build and lead our development team.

You're probably a great fit if you...

have strong experience with React and modern JavaScript or TypeScript development.
are comfortable working across frontend, backend, APIs and databases.
have a solid understanding of data pipelines, event tracking and analytics infrastructure.
understand cloud infrastructure, deployment and scalable software architecture.
can balance technical excellence with the realities of an early-stage startup.
are interested in the business behind the product, not just the technology.
are naturally curious, entrepreneurial and comfortable challenging assumptions.
know when to build something properly and when not to spend three weeks engineering a button.

Experience with mobile applications, React Native, consumer-facing platforms or early-stage startups is definitely a plus.

Equity ownership:

Real technical ownership:
Define the architecture, technical strategy and engineering direction.

Participate in key product, business and strategic decisions as part of the founding team.
Flexibility:
A part-time, primarily remote working arrangement.
Room to grow:
Build and lead your own engineering team as the company scales.
Technical freedom:
Make meaningful technology decisions without unnecessary corporate bureaucracy.
A great team:
Ambitious people who take their work seriously without taking themselves too seriously.

We're an early-stage startup, and this position is currently compensated through equity rather than a salary.
We're offering equity
because we're looking for a genuine founding partner who wants to help shape the company and participate in its long-term success.

We're not simply looking for a developer. We're looking for someone who wants to build something they can genuinely call their own.

Let's build something cool.

You don't need to know every programming language or have spent the last ten years working at Google.

We're more interested in your ability to solve problems, make smart technical decisions, understand the bigger picture and actually get things done.

new_jobs.description:
Founding CTO | Ditto 🚀

Are you interested in making technical decisions without needing to convince five managers, two architects and someone from finance? Then keep reading!

About Ditto

We're Ditto, a Toronto-based tech startup building a consumer mobile app designed to make everyday life a little more connected.

We are preparing for a new phase of our product and are looking for a technical leader to join our founding team, take ownership of our technology and help us build a scalable, data-driven platform.
We're a small team with big ambitions, and we're looking for someone who wants to build a company, not just write code.

Who we're looking for

We're looking for a hands-on CTO with a strong technical background, an entrepreneurial mindset and the ability to turn business and product ambitions into solid technical solutions.

Ideally, you're a full-stack developer
who's comfortable working across the entire technology stack, from building intuitive user experiences to designing backend architecture and data infrastructure.

Our technology stack is built around React
, and we're particularly interested in someone with a strong understanding of data pipelines, event tracking and product analytics.

We don't just want to build features. We want to understand how people use them, why they use them and how we can make them better.

What you'll be doing

Technical Strategy:
Own and define Ditto's technical vision, architecture and technology roadmap.
Full-Stack Development:
Actively contribute to frontend and backend development, integrations and infrastructure.
React Development:
Maintain, improve and expand our existing application.
Data Architecture & Pipelines:
Design reliable infrastructure for collecting, processing, storing and leveraging product data.
Event Tracking & Analytics:
Implement tracking mechanisms that enable us to understand user behaviour, engagement, conversion and retention.
Scalability:
Build a technical foundation that supports our growth without needing to rebuild everything six months later.
Security & Reliability:
Ensure our platform follows sound practices around security, privacy, performance and maintainability.
Product Collaboration:
Work closely with the product and marketing teams to translate business objectives into technical solutions.
Technical Leadership:
Shape our engineering culture and eventually build and lead our development team.

You're probably a great fit if you...

have strong experience with React and modern JavaScript or TypeScript development.
are comfortable working across frontend, backend, APIs and databases.
have a solid understanding of data pipelines, event tracking and analytics infrastructure.
understand cloud infrastructure, deployment and scalable software architecture.
can balance technical excellence with the realities of an early-stage startup.
are interested in the business behind the product, not just the technology.
are naturally curious, entrepreneurial and comfortable challenging assumptions.
know when to build something properly and when not to spend three weeks engineering a button.

Experience with mobile applications, React Native, consumer-facing platforms or early-stage startups is definitely a plus.

What's in it for you?

Equity ownership:
A meaningful stake in the company, depending on your experience, commitment and responsibilities.
Real technical ownership:
Define the architecture, technical strategy and engineering direction.
A seat at the table:
Participate in key product, business and strategic decisions as part of the founding team.
Flexibility:
A part-time, primarily remote working arrangement.
Room to grow:
Build and lead your own engineering team as the company scales.
Technical freedom:
Make meaningful technology decisions without unnecessary corporate bureaucracy.
A great team:
Ambitious people who take their work seriously without taking themselves too seriously.

A little transparency

We're an early-stage startup, and this position is currently compensated through equity rather than a salary.
We're offering equity
because we're looking for a genuine founding partner who wants to help shape the company and participate in its long-term success.

We're not simply looking for a developer. We're looking for someone who wants to build something they can genuinely call their own.

Let's build something cool.

You don't need to know every programming language or have spent the last ten years working at Google.

We're more interested in your ability to solve problems, make smart technical decisions, understand the bigger picture and actually get things done.

If you're excited about building a product, shaping a company's future and being part of an entrepreneurial journey, we'd love to hear from you.

To be the benchmark in private healthcare.

OUR VALUES

Passion | Respect | Integrity | Commitment | Innovation.

The Mandate

In a context of sustained growth and transformation of its activities, Lacroix Medical Group is seeking a Director of Information Technology who will actively contribute to the organization's technological evolution.

Reporting directly to the President and CEO, the Director of IT plays a strategic role across the entire network. They are responsible for defining, structuring, and developing the IT function to effectively support the organization's operations, growth, and ambitions.

They provide leadership for technology strategy, infrastructure, business systems, cybersecurity, data governance, digital transformation, and artificial intelligence.

He is also responsible for the performance of his team and the organization's technology partner ecosystem. Performance and Business Continuity

Ensure the performance, robustness, and high availability of the infrastructure and technology platforms essential to the network's medical and administrative activities, including ERP, CRM, DME, LIS, SaaS, and cloud environments.

Digital Transformation, Data, and Artificial Intelligence

Identify and prioritize initiatives to transform the organization through technology, data valorization, automation, and artificial intelligence. Lead major technology projects and ensure their effective integration into operations.

Cybersecurity and Risk Management

Maintain high standards in cybersecurity, information protection, redundancy, and business continuity in an environment where system availability and the protection of medical data are critical.

Leadership and Organizational Performance

Lead and develop a competent, autonomous, and accountable IT team. Establish clear objectives and performance indicators, ensure rigorous budget management, and optimize the contribution of suppliers, consultants, and technology partners.

An Executive Role Close to Operations

At Lacroix Medical Group, technology must meet the realities on the ground.

The IT Director will therefore need to maintain close contact with the various business units and network teams to understand their needs, anticipate challenges, and ensure that technological solutions contribute concretely to operational performance and service quality.

The position consequently requires excellent mobility. The successful candidate will be required to travel regularly throughout the Lacroix network in Quebec to meet with teams, support projects, and remain connected to the operational realities of the various facilities.

This on-the-ground presence is an essential component of the role and not an occasional responsibility.

The mandate expressly includes regular visits to service points.

A bachelor's degree in computer engineering, computer science, or a related field;
15 to 20 years of experience in information technology, including a minimum of 5 years in a management role;
Mastery of software architecture and project management;
A solid understanding of multi-site and cloud infrastructures;
Good knowledge of SaaS environments and major business platforms: ERP, CRM, financial systems, telephony, Microsoft 365, and others;
A thorough understanding of the issues cybersecurity, data governance and valorization, and artificial intelligence;
Proven experience in team management and development;
Recognized leadership in transformation and change management;
Ability to prioritize, make decisions, and manage effectively in a complex and evolving environment;
Excellent business acumen and the ability to communicate technological issues to senior management;
Fluency in French and English, both written and spoken;
A valid driver's license, a vehicle, and significant availability for regular travel throughout the network.
